training: All four arms reached cumulative epoch 100; epoch-0100 checkpoints and W&B resume artifacts were committed before the failure.
failure_signature: run_engram.py:275 np.testing.assert_allclose -> AssertionError: Not equal to tolerance rtol=0, atol=1e-07
what_the_check_does: Reloads selected checkpoint (model_min_ebops.keras; no arm met the 350k budget), re-predicts validation, requires AUC and accuracy to equal the in-training values within 1e-7.

evidence_by_gpu.result: FAIL on AUC only (d_auc=-1.5e-6); accuracy reproduced exactly

evidence_by_gpu.gpu: unknown (logs no longer contain GPU line)

diagnosis: Not a node lottery. FP32-only GPUs (Turing/Volta) reproduce the logged accuracy exactly; every Ampere/Ada GPU returns one identical, different value (|d_acc| 1.3e-4..2.7e-4 = 16..33 of 124,000 jets), even in the pod that trained the model. The saved model is therefore correct; the reload+predict path computes with different arithmetic on TF32-capable GPUs than the in-training evaluation did.
hypothesis_not_yet_tested: TF32 matmul in the fresh load_model+predict path. Why the in-training predict on the same Ampere card matches FP32 hardware is NOT established.
secondary_finding: atol=1e-7 on macro AUC is tighter than cross-architecture FP32 reproducibility (E01 on 2080 Ti missed by 1.5e-6 with accuracy exact; E03 on V100 passed by luck at 4.8e-8). Accuracy granularity is 1/124000 = 8.1e-6.
